claim.quote: The spectrum extends up to energies of 80 TeV and is well matched by model calculations in the framework of inverse Compton scattering of various seed photons in the nebula

name: HEGRA measures the Crab Nebula spectrum from 500 GeV to 80 TeV

summary.plain: Nearly 400 hours of HEGRA data on the Crab Nebula give its gamma-ray spectrum from 500 GeV up to 80 TeV, well matched by inverse-Compton models, with an average magnetic field of about 160 microgauss in the nebula.
summary.technical: Close to 400 hours of useful stereoscopic data from 1997 to 2002; spectrum to 80 TeV matched by inverse-Compton models including a compact mm-wave emission region; average magnetic field (161.6 +- 0.8 stat +- 18 sys) microgauss; emission region position shifted 13 arcsec west of the pulsar.

title: The Crab Nebula and Pulsar between 500 GeV and 80 TeV: Observations with the HEGRA stereoscopic air Cherenkov telescopes
why_it_matters: The abstract says the presence of protons in the nebula is not required to explain the observed flux.
